title: x-unraid
description: Presentation metadata carried inside an ordinary compose file. Validates the x-unraid blocks and permits every other compose key, so it can be run against a whole compose file converted to JSON. Validate the SOURCE file converted to JSON, not `docker compose config` output, which has a history of stripping extension fields. There is nothing here for individual form fields: what a value is for is written in the comment beside it, which YAML already has and this schema cannot see.
$comment: format: "uri" throughout this schema is documentation only — Draft 2020-12 treats "format" as a non-enforcing annotation unless the validator is given an optional RFC-3986/3987 checker package, which this project does not install. The actual gate on every address-shaped key below is its "pattern", not its "format".

stack.$comment: additionalProperties is deliberately absent (see docs/x-unraid-schema.md, Validation): reading rule 1 already commits to ignoring unknown keys so a file written for a later schema version still renders on an older StaXX. A propertyNames pattern was weighed and rejected — a typo like overvieww is still a perfectly shaped property name, so a shape check would not catch the thing it is meant to catch, and would only put a second, narrower key format in competition with the same forward-compatibility promise.

version.description: Schema version. A reader seeing a higher major version falls back to inference rather than misreading the metadata.

category.description: Unraid's existing category taxonomy, e.g. MediaApp:Video.

sections.description: Form sections a service has switched off, keyed by service name then by compose key (healthcheck, ports, deploy.resources, cap_add…). Each entry is either the boolean false — hidden, holding nothing — or a string holding JSON ({"after":…,"lines":[…]}), the section's own lines kept verbatim so re-enabling it restores them byte for byte. The JSON inside that string is deliberately not validated here: it is not YAML, so it is one opaque line to this schema, not a second copy of the compose structure. If the compose file itself still has the block, the file wins and a leftover entry here is ignored.

icon.description: Four accepted forms, told apart by their shape: a full http(s) URL; a path relative to the stack directory, e.g. ./icon.png; a name from the selfh.st icon collection, e.g. jellyfin; or a Font Awesome glyph, e.g. fa-database, which is what Unraid's own XML templates accept. Omit it and the icon is matched automatically from the container's image name. The pattern only rules out shapes that are none of these — e.g. a path climbing out of the stack directory with ../ — it does not confirm a selfh.st name or a file actually exist.

service.$comment: additionalProperties absent for the same reason as $defs/stack — see the $comment there.

project.description: This service's own project page, when it differs from the stack's — a repository belongs to an image, and a stack can hold several. Falls back to the stack-level key of the same name when absent.

support.description: This service's own support page (a forum thread, an issue tracker). Falls back to the stack-level key of the same name when absent.

webui.description: Link to the container's web interface. Supports Unraid's [IP] substitution. A literal port written in the address, e.g. http://[IP]:80/, is used as-is. A [PORT:nnnn] token is an older shape kept for files written before the port was typed in directly; its own number is not read, and StaXX instead works the port out from the service's first ports entry, taking whichever side of it actually answers: the host-facing side on a bridge network, or the container's own side on host networking or macvlan/ipvlan, where nothing is published.

display.description: Stored, but nothing acts on it yet. The intent is that 'advanced' will fold a sidecar such as a database behind the form's advanced toggle.

update.description: Overrides the stack-level update block for this service alone; falls back to it, then to the global setting, when absent.

network_stash.description: A clipboard, not a description of anything: written only by the network-mode picker, and read only when that same control is asked to restore it. Holds this service's own networks: block exactly as it stood before network_mode replaced it — a JSON object holding the block's own lines verbatim (comments, fixed addresses and all) rather than read into values and rebuilt, plus the name of the key it followed so it goes back in the same place. Both halves matter: a restore that rebuilt the lines would lose the comments, and one that ignored the position would reorder the file. Together they make a set-aside and a restore byte-for-byte. Not validated as YAML here for the same reason sections' own stash is not: it is one opaque string to this schema, not a second copy of the compose structure. Meaningless, and ignored, on a service that is not currently using network_mode.

update.description: How this stack (or one service in it) should be kept up to date. Every key optional; an absent key inherits from the level below it — service, then stack, then the plugin's global setting.

mode.description: off = never apply on its own. notify = show that an update was found but never apply it automatically. auto = apply it once the delay below has passed.

delay.description: Hours to wait, after an update is first seen, before an 'auto' mode applies it.
